Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot inference be made inductive, scoring each image only with statistics of the K normal support images and source-validation data instead of test-set min-max normalisation, while keeping image AUROC within 1 point of the re-run transductive baseline and making each image's score invariant to the composition of the rest of the test set (prevalence 10-50%, with and without outliers)? The replacement is evaluated component by component (normalisation, then fusion weight, then image-level aggregation), with sensitivity at 95% specificity and expected calibration error reported alongside AUROC.
Target paper title: Adapting Visual-Language Models for Generalizable Anomaly Detection in Medical Images
Target paper abstract: Recent advancements in large-scale visual-language pre-trained models have led to significant progress in zero-/few-shot anomaly detection within natural image domains. However, the substantial domain divergence between natural and medical images limits the effectiveness of these methodologies in medical anomaly detection. This paper introduces a novel lightweight multi-level adaptation and comparison framework to repurpose the CLIP model for medical anomaly detection. Our approach integrates multiple residual adapters into the pre-trained visual encoder, enabling a stepwise enhancement of visual features across different levels. This multi-level adaptation is guided by multi-level, pixel-wise visual-language feature alignment loss functions, which recalibrate the model's focus from object semantics in natural imagery to anomaly identification in medical images. The adapted features exhibit improved generalization across various medical data types, even in zero-shot scenarios where the model encounters unseen medical modalities and anatomical regions during training. Our experiments on medical anomaly detection benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly surpasses current state-of-the-art models, with an average AUC improvement of 6.24% and 7.33% for anomaly classification, 2.03% and 2.37% for anomaly segmentation, under the zero-shot and few-shot settings, respectively. Source code is available at: https://github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD

The research idea:
TITLE: Weighted conformal scoring that borrows source-modality normals to stabilise small support sets
SUMMARY: Enlarge the leave-one-out reference set of the few-shot branch at small K by adding normal source-modality images, weighted by their feature similarity to the target supports (weighted conformal prediction), so per-image p-values remain fine-grained and valid under modality shift.
HYPOTHESIS: At K = 2 and K = 4, weighted conformal p-values using similarity-weighted source normals reduce the variance of image AUROC across support draws by at least 40% and keep the realised false-positive rate within 3 points of the nominal 5%, whereas unweighted support-only conformal p-values have a resolution of 1/(K + 1) and cannot reach 5% at K = 2.
RATIONALE: Both parents rely on the K target supports for their reference distribution, which is too coarse at K = 2 (p-values cannot fall below 1/3). A different mechanism, suggested by the conformal parent's guarantee and the isotonic parent's use of source data, is to borrow normal reference scores from source modalities and correct for the modality shift with likelihood-ratio weights, as in weighted conformal prediction under covariate shift (Tibshirani et al., 2019). Weights are estimated from how similar each source normal's global feature is to the target supports, so similar source anatomy contributes more. This keeps per-image scoring inductive while fixing the small-K resolution problem that limits both parents.
METHOD: 1) Source reference pool: few-shot scores of 500 normal validation images per source modality, each scored against the target support bank (as a target image would be). 2) Weights: w_j = exp(-||g_j - g_supp||^2/(2 h^2)) with g the mean CLS feature at level 4, g_supp the mean of target supports, h = median pairwise distance; support LOO scores get weight 1 (normalised so their total weight equals that of the source pool when K >= 8, and 25% when K = 2). 3) Weighted p-value p = (sum_{i: r_i >= s} w_i + w_test)/(sum_i w_i + w_test). 4) Combine with the zero-shot branch in log-odds as in the conformal parent. 5) test_few.py: implement; remove min-max. No adapter training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support z-score. Conditions: support-only conformal; unweighted source pool; weighted source pool. Metrics: realised FPR at p <= 0.05 per K, variance of AUROC across support draws, image AUROC, score shift under resampling. Falsified if weighting does not reduce AUROC variance by 40% at K <= 4 or if realised FPR exceeds 8%.
